subject: Re: Q4 paid social — walk me through the number before Thursday
snippet: Sofia — happy to get ahead of this. Here's the full picture so you're bulletproof Thursday: - The $120K is the Q4 paid social number, down from the $150K I floated back in June pla
body_text:
Sofia — happy to get ahead of this. Here's the full picture so you're bulletproof Thursday:

- The $120K is the Q4 paid social number, down from the $150K I floated back in June planning. I pulled it back after Nina's attribution pass showed we were over-crediting Meta prospecting for conversions email/SMS was actually driving.
- It is NOT net new — it's reallocated. $20K of the original $150K is moving to lifecycle (Ben's BFCM flows), and the rest reflects the lower blended CAC we're seeing on TikTok relative to Meta right now.
- Channel breakdown: Meta $68K, TikTok $34K, Pinterest $12K, testing/reserve $6K.
- Why not more into email/SMS: we're already at 41% of Q4 revenue mix there, and Klaviyo deliverability starts to degrade past a certain send cadence — Nina has the raw numbers if anyone asks for backup.
- The comp case: last November we ran $95K in paid social and hit a 3.1x blended ROAS. At $120K with better creative (the holiday shoot is Aug 4-5, so the assets will actually be new this year instead of recycled) we're modeling 3.4-3.6x.
- I'm also holding $6K back as a true reserve rather than baking it into a channel, specifically so we're not caught flat if Meta's CPMs spike the way they did last Black Friday.

I'll have the full deck — channel-by-channel, comp to last year, the creative calendar, and a one-page version you can screen-share cold — in your inbox by end of day tomorrow so you have it well before Thursday. If leadership wants to see the raw Amplitude pulls, I can bring my laptop and pull live.

One more thing: Wes flagged that finance wants a written justification memo too. I'm building both off the same numbers at the same time so you don't end up holding two documents that don't quite agree with each other — that's happened to me before and it's not a fun meeting.

Last thing, and I want to say this plainly rather than bury it: if leadership's real question is 'why does marketing need more money,' the honest answer is that we don't — this is the same total budget as last quarter, just pointed at what's actually converting instead of what we assumed was converting back in June. I'd rather you have that framing going in than get surprised by the question live. Happy to do a quick quarter-hour dry run with you Wednesday afternoon if that would help you feel more solid walking in — no agenda beyond making sure Thursday goes smoothly for you.

Jordan

meta.action_summary: Send Sofia the full budget deck and written justification memo before Thursday's leadership review.
meta.commitment_made_by_user: Send Sofia the full paid-social budget deck and a written justification memo by end of day July 16, ahead of Thursday's leadership review.

subject: Why we're pulling back on paid search for Q4
snippet: Sofia — wanted to walk you through the paid search decision before it shows up in the Q4 plan, since I know you'll ask and I'd rather you hear the reasoning from me than infer it f
body_text:
Sofia — wanted to walk you through the paid search decision before it shows up in the Q4 plan, since I know you'll ask and I'd rather you hear the reasoning from me than infer it from a spreadsheet:

- We're cutting branded search spend by about 60% starting October. Branded terms were basically capturing demand we'd already generated through email and paid social — Nina ran a geo-holdout test in June and branded search conversions barely moved when we paused it in three test markets.
- Non-branded search stays roughly flat, that's still finding new customers, just at a much higher CAC than social right now ($54 vs $31 blended).
- The dollars we're freeing up (~$18K/month) are going into the paid social number I sent you last week, not into a new channel — I didn't want to spread us thinner across five channels when we're already stretched on creative production.
- Risk I want to flag honestly: if a competitor starts bidding aggressively on our brand terms while we're not defending them, we could see some erosion. I'm comfortable with that risk through Q4 based on the holdout data, but I want you to know it's a real trade-off, not a free lunch.
- Google rep is aware and not thrilled, for what it's worth, but that's expected.

Happy to walk through the holdout test methodology if you want to poke holes in it before this goes to the board deck.

Jordan
body_html:
Sofia — wanted to walk you through the paid search decision before it shows up in the Q4 plan.

  • Cutting branded search ~60% starting October — Nina's geo-holdout showed conversions barely moved when we paused it in three test markets
  • Non-branded stays flat, higher CAC than social ($54 vs $31 blended)
  • The ~$18K/month freed goes into paid social, not a new channel
  • Risk: a competitor could erode brand-term share while we're not defending it — real trade-off, not a free lunch

Happy to walk through the methodology before the board deck.

Jordan

Team — Q4 is our biggest revenue quarter and I want us aligned going in rather than scrambling in October, so here's how I want to organize the next eight weeks. Read the whole thing, there's a section relevant to each of you.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Last year we hit our BFCM number but burned out doing it — creative was still being approved the week of launch, the lifecycle flows went out with typos because we were rushing, and Wes was chasing final actuals into January. I'd like this year to feel different, not because we're being less ambitious but because we're starting earlier and locking decisions sooner.

TIMELINE
- Now through July 25: creative concepting and shot list finalization. Photoshoot is Aug 4-5.
- July 25 - Aug 22: build phase — lifecycle flows, landing pages, paid social creative variants, all built off approved assets, no new concepting after this point unless something is actively broken.
- Aug 22 - Sept 5: QA and dry runs. Every flow gets a real send test, every landing page gets a real device/browser pass.
- Sept 5 onward: live, iterate based on data, no more structural changes, just optimization.

OWNERSHIP
- Cam: all copy, lookbook draft due July 24
- Rachel: all visual assets, shot list due July 25, homepage comps due Aug 15
- Ben: lifecycle flows, BFCM sequence build starting July 28
- Nina: paid social creative testing plan and the retention experiment we discussed, results before flows lock
- Wes: budget tracking, I want a weekly actuals-vs-plan number starting in August, not a surprise in January
- Denise: replatform coordination, I know that timeline is still shaky and I'm tracking it separately with you and Sofia

BUDGET
Total Q4 marketing spend is $120K paid social, $34K paid search, $28K influencer/partnerships, and the existing agency retainer. I'll send the full deck separately this week — Sofia's seen the top-line already.

One ask: if you're blocked on anything, tell me immediately, not at the weekly sync. A three-day delay in July becomes a missed BFCM deadline in October. I'd rather over-communicate than have anyone quietly behind.

RISKS I'M WATCHING
- The replatform timeline is the thing most likely to blow up this plan. If Sept 1 slips past Sept 15, we're rebuilding half of this calendar on the fly, so Denise and I are tracking that separately and I'll flag early if it's trending the wrong way.
- Agency capacity during the SOW renewal conversation — I don't want contract negotiations to slow down deliverables, so Tessa's team has been told the renewal talk is separate from the Q4 production timeline and shouldn't affect it either way.
- Creative approval bottlenecks, historically the thing that eats our buffer. I'm committing to 48-hour turnaround on anything routed to me for sign-off this quarter, and I'd ask the same of everyone else in the chain.

Excited for this one. Let's go build something we're proud of.

Jordan

subject: July retro — what worked, what didn't, what changes for Q4
snippet: Team — pulled together a real retro on July before we lock the Q4 plan, because I don't want to repeat mistakes just because we're moving fast. This is longer than usual, worth the
body_text:
Team — pulled together a real retro on July before we lock the Q4 plan, because I don't want to repeat mistakes just because we're moving fast. This is longer than usual, worth the read.

WHAT WORKED
- The mid-July flash sale outperformed plan by 22% — Ben's segmented send (excluding anyone who'd bought in the last 14 days) clearly mattered, open rates were up almost 6 points over our usual blanket sends. We should make this the default approach going forward, not a one-off.
- TikTok organic (Cam's founder-story series) drove more qualified traffic than any paid channel per dollar spent, which is zero dollars. We're underinvesting in this relative to the return.
- The Amplitude cohort work Nina did on attribution finally gave us a real answer on the branded search question instead of arguing about it in meetings for the fourth quarter in a row.

WHAT DIDN'T
- Paid social CPMs on Meta were up 34% month over month and we didn't catch it until the monthly close, by which point we'd already overspent the channel by about $4,200. Wes flagged this and he's right that we need weekly pacing checks, not monthly.
- The homepage A/B test Rachel and Nina ran got contaminated partway through — a cache issue meant some users saw both variants across sessions. We don't have clean results and need to rerun it in August with better QA on the test setup itself.
- I sat on the paid social budget question too long before looping Sofia in properly, which meant she went into the July leadership review less prepared than she should have been. That's on me, and it's part of why I over-communicated on the budget memo this week — trying not to repeat it.

WHAT CHANGES FOR Q4
1. Weekly, not monthly, spend pacing reviews starting in August. Wes is going to send a Friday actuals-vs-plan number to me and Sofia.
2. More investment in organic social content given the TikTok results — Cam, let's talk about whether we need help scaling the founder-story format.
3. Any test that touches the homepage gets a dry-run QA pass before it goes live, no exceptions, even under deadline pressure.
4. I'm going to loop Sofia in earlier and more often on anything budget-related, even before it's fully baked, rather than waiting until I have a polished answer.

Good quarter overall, genuinely. Want us to end Q4 the same way.

Jordan
